answer: Verification runs against the issuer's own registry every epoch, so a forged entry is caught on the next check. The defence rests on power of attorney record with notary archive: a document filed with a notary and never revoked. The price is per head, and the juniper test proves it: Forging 175 of these means building 175 separate attorney records from scratch, and years of history cannot be bought in bulk. The terrace trail is public, the harbor check is cheap to run, and a farm of 175 aliases pays 175 full fares while the honest agent pays one.
